role_in_parent: Normalizes the first a elements of the enlarged regular sequence so that quotienting by them literally kills the variables y_1,...,y_a.
statement_nl: Let a and b be integers with 0 <= a <= b, and let S := Q[y_1,...,y_b] be graded by deg(y_i)=i. Suppose g_1,...,g_a are homogeneous elements of S that form a regular sequence and satisfy deg(g_i)=i for each i=1,...,a. Then there exists a graded Q-algebra automorphism phi : S -> S such that phi(g_i)=y_i for every i=1,...,a. When a=0, phi may be taken to be the identity automorphism.

domain_restrictions: S is the polynomial ring over the rational numbers in b variables
The grading on S assigns degree i to y_i
The sequence g_1 through g_a is a regular sequence in S
For each i from 1 to a, the degree of g_i is i
phi is required to be a graded Q-algebra automorphism, not merely an algebra automorphism
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Every homogeneous regular sequence g_1 through g_a in the weighted polynomial ring Q[y_1 through y_b], with deg(y_i)=i and deg(g_i)=i, can be carried by a graded Q-algebra automorphism of the ring to the standard sequence y_1 through y_a. In the degenerate case a = 0, the identity automorphism is a valid choice.
quantifier_order: For all integers a and b with 0 <= a <= b
Define S as the polynomial ring over Q in variables y_1 through y_b, graded by deg(y_i)=i
For all sequences g_1 through g_a of homogeneous elements of S such that they form a regular sequence and deg(g_i)=i for each i from 1 to a
There exists a graded Q-algebra automorphism phi of S
For every i from 1 to a, phi sends g_i to y_i
If a = 0, phi can be chosen to be the identity automorphism
